question.text: A hydrogen-like atom (described by the Bohr model) is observed to emit six wavelengths, originating from all possible transitions between a group of levels. These levels have energies between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>85</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> and<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>544</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> (including both these values). Find the atomic number of the atom. (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>hc</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1240</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>, ground state energy of hydrogen atom = <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math>)

solution.text:
Total 6 lines are emitted. Therefore,

n(n-1)2=6

or n = 4

So, transition is taking place between mth energy state and (m + 3)th energy state.

Em = - 0. 85 eV

Or

-13.6(z2m2)=-0.85

Or

zm= 0. 25 ... (i)

Similarly, Em + 3 = - 0. 544 eV

or -13.6z2(m+3)2 = - 0. 544

or z(m+3)=0.2…(ii) ...(ii)

Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii) for z and m, we get

m = 12 and z = 3
